newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Interstate to meet Q2 estimates.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Interstate to meet Q2 estimates.

text.p: Interstate Hotels Co president and chief executive officer W. Thomas Parrington Jr. expects the company to meet or beat second quarter earnings estimates of $0.33 a share.
"I think we'll be meeting or exceeding the First Call estimates," Parrington told Reuters about the company's second quarter earnings to be issued tomorrow.
Parrington also was comfortable with earnings estimates of $1.18 per share for 1997.

Interstate, a hotel and hotel management company conducted its initial public offering in June 1996 and a secondary offering in December, reported a 1996 loss of $1.6 million, including charges for extraordinary items.

On a proforma basis, Interstate's 1996 net income totaled $32.9 million, or $0.93 a share, on $477.5 million in sales. Proforma results give effect to the initial public offering and the company's acquisitions.
Parrington said the company is aiming for 20 to 25 percent growth in annual revenues and total rooms.
Interstate manages, leases or owns 230 hotels with a total of 45,000 rooms.
The hotels are in the upscale or luxury categories and are under 25 different brands including Hilton Hotels, ITT Corp's Sheraton and Marriott International Inc.

The hotel company boasts an average occupancy rate in the mid to high 70 percent range, compared with an industry-wide average of 65.8 percent, according to Coopers & Lybrand's Lodging and Gaming Group.

While there is a building boom in moderate and budget hotels, Parrington said there should be an equilibrium in supply and demand for luxury hotel construction and purchasing for the next three to five years.
Interstate is in an alliance with Equity Inns Inc, accounting for 89 of the properties that Interstate manages. Equity Inns Inc is a real estate investment trust.
Parrington said the company derives its management revenues from revenues performance and profitability of the hotels and has the rights to set the rights and marketing plan for the properties.
Since the initial public offering, Interstate has also acquired 18 hotels with an aggregate value of $550 million.
The company has a team of 10 executives that scout for real estate deals that are not extensively marketed and represent a good value or offer prospects for increased worth, Parrington said.
